findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: If term->osc_string contains a malicious payload that could be interpreted as a command
findings.assumptions: The code fragment is part of a larger application where term->osc_string can be influenced by user input or external sources. The data from term->osc_string is directly copied to the clipboard without further validation or sanitization.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: If term->osc_string contains a base64 encoded payload that, when decoded, could be interpreted as a command
findings.assumptions: The code assumes that the data in term->osc_string is safe to decode and use without further validation. There is no check to ensure that the decoded data does not contain harmful commands.

findings.title: Buffer Over-read / Buffer Over-write ('Stack Buffer Overflow')
findings.trigger: If term->osc_string is manipulated to be longer than expected, it could lead to a buffer over-read or over-write
findings.assumptions: The code does not validate the length of term->osc_string before passing it to base64_decode_block. If term->osc_string is too long, it could lead to accessing memory outside the allocated buffer.

findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: If term->osc_string contains a malicious payload that could be interpreted as a command when pasted
findings.assumptions: The code places the decoded data directly into the clipboard. If this data is later pasted into an application that interprets it as a command, it could lead to command execution.
